clue.text: Policeman arresting Henry on crack quickly

indicators.note: to arrest someone is to hold them, so the policeman wraps round Henry

blocks.note: a crack or blow, as in a karate chop
slang for a police officer
H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A police officer nabs a man called Henry who is high on crack cocaine, and does it fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' reads as the drug, but here it is a blow; H is the symbol for the henry, the SI unit of inductance.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop-chop is an informal exclamation urging someone to hurry up.

clue.text: That male sheep is angry

blocks.note: the pronoun for a male person
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A ram in a field is in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'male sheep' looks like one unit, but 'male' joins 'That' to give the pronoun and 'sheep' alone gives the ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Het up is an informal adjective for agitated or upset, so it fits angry.

clue.text: Long number that's secret and ending in three?

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of three is kept

blocks.note: a personal identification number is kept secret
the final letter of the word three

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a long secret code that finishes with the digit three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective for the number, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine for something is to long or yearn for it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Old ink in edited photo is matter of controversy

indicators.note: an edited picture has been altered and rearranged, so the letters of photo are reordered
one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
tat is slang for a tattoo, a piece of ink
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An old tattoo inserted into a retouched photograph causes a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Tat is a slang clipping of tattoo, and 'ink' is modern slang for tattoos generally.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a contentious issue that everyone is reluctant to handle.

clue.text: Statement I put in letters

indicators.note: to put something in a thing is to place it inside, so I goes within

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters delivered to your door are the post

explanation.surface: Someone describes a written declaration they enclosed in their correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a posit is a proposition or assertion put forward as a basis for argument.

clue.text: Assert sea-creature's in control of current

indicators.note: something in control of another holds it, so the creature wraps round it

blocks.note: a clam is a shellfish of the sea
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a marine animal steers an ocean current.
explanation.definitionFit: To claim something is to state it as true, a direct synonym of assert.

clue.text: Light up repeatedly - man chokes terribly having inhaled one

indicators.note: doing something terribly means doing it badly, so the words are mangled into a new order
breathing something in takes it inside, so one goes within the letters

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A smoker who keeps lighting cigarettes splutters badly after taking a drag.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes in among the letters and the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To chain-smoke is to light each cigarette from the last, smoking continuously.

clue.text: A spray of liquid's absorbed by grass when no longer needing heat?

indicators.note: something absorbed is soaked up inside another thing, so the spray goes within the grass

blocks.note: taken as written
a fine spray of droplets is a mist
rice is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: Watering a lawn when the weather turns cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: The heat here is the heat of battle; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a truce, the point when fighting stops and the heat of war is no longer wanted.

clue.text: Model being married on boat

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for married
Noah's ark was a boat; 'on' places it after

explanation.surface: A fashion model gets married aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a catwalk, but it means a version of a product.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark is a particular version or design of a machine, as in a Mark II car.

clue.text: Author's written about two beastly males shot in the sky

indicators.note: about signals turning round, so the word for author is read backwards

blocks.note: to author something is to pen it
a hog is a male pig
the second of the two beastly males: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A writer describes two male animals being shot from the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Two male animals, a hog and a ram, follow the reversed pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephogram is a photograph of clouds, a picture shot of the sky.

clue.text: Put out lewd message with opening censored in court

indicators.note: censoring the opening removes the first letter of the message

blocks.note: a sext is a sexually explicit text message
taken as written
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Someone sends an indecent message, partly redacted, that ends up as evidence in a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Extinct describes a fire that has been put out, as well as a species that has died out.

clue.text: Three months you ultimately spent guarding Los Angeles prison

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept
something spent is used up and gone, so that letter is taken away
a guard surrounds what it protects, so the shortened season wraps round the city

blocks.note: summer is a season of three months
the last letter of you
LA is the abbreviation for Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Someone serves a three-month sentence in a Los Angeles jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' reads as time served, but it removes the letter just chosen; 'Three months' is a season, not a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Slammer is slang for a jail, from the slam of the cell door.

clue.text: Desire opening of poppies, primroses or pansies in garden

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: whichever flower is chosen, the first letter is the same
to hoe is to work in a garden

explanation.surface: A gardener longs to see the first flowers come up in the beds.
explanation.walkthrough: All three flowers begin with the same letter, so the list is a playful way to give one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope is a wish or longing for something, a close synonym of desire.

clue.text: Satisfied with small section of book

blocks.note: content means happy or satisfied
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A reader is pleased with a short part of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The contents is the page listing chapters at the front of a book.

clue.text: Outlaw master alcohol ingredient

blocks.note: M is an abbreviation for master
ale is an alcoholic drink
a factor is a contributing element or ingredient

explanation.surface: A chemist identifies the key component in an alcoholic drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' reads like a verb meaning ban, but it is the noun for a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer or criminal, someone who breaks the law.

clue.text: Dinosaur dung spreading, I assume

indicators.note: something spreading pushes apart what surrounds it, so it sits between the other words

blocks.note: taken as written
guano is the droppings of seabirds or bats
to don clothes is to put them on, or assume them

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a pile of droppings came from a dinosaur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I assume' reads as a hedge, but 'I' and 'assume' are separate pieces with the dung pushed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur, an example of the category.

clue.text: Trap John on the way back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: both john and bog are slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A man called John is caught in an ambush on his return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' is not a name but slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap and gob are both slang words for the mouth.

clue.text: Surprise kissogram's outside bakery with no clothes offering better service

definitions.note: describes the bookmaker; read as 'one offering a service to betters'

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its two end letters
stripping off the clothes removes the outer layer, leaving only the inside letters

blocks.note: boo is a cry made to startle someone
the first and last letters of kissogram
bakery without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A naked kissogram turns up outside a bakery as a surprise, offering a superior service.
explanation.walkthrough: A better here is one who bets, not the comparative of good.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker takes wagers, providing a service to gamblers who bet.

clue.text: A horse charging violently causing characters to relocate

blocks.note: taken as written
a nag is an old horse
ramming is crashing into something with force

explanation.surface: A horse stampedes and makes the people in a story move away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' are letters, not people in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Making an anagram moves letters into new positions, so anagramming relocates characters.

clue.text: Helping to look after university in state of collapse

indicators.note: looking after someone means keeping them safe within your care, so the portion wraps round

blocks.note: a helping is a portion, or ration
U is the abbreviation for university
taken as written

explanation.surface: Supporting a university in a country falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in state' looks like one phrase, but 'in' belongs to the wordplay and 'state of collapse' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruination is the condition of being ruined or destroyed, a state of collapse.

clue.text: Something that needs discussing with king after OPEC obtain liquid

indicators.note: a liquid has no fixed shape, so these letters flow into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
K is the abbreviation for king, placed after

explanation.surface: A king follows the oil cartel's lead in securing petroleum, a topic for debate.
explanation.walkthrough: OPEC is the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, so 'obtain liquid' looks like oil, but liquid is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a bone to pick means having a grievance that must be talked over with someone.

clue.text: Date's wild when stripping

indicators.note: stripping takes off the outer layer, so only the inside letters remain

blocks.note: feral means wild; its inner letters are kept

explanation.surface: Someone's romantic partner gets carried away while undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date' suggests a romantic partner, but it means a period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A date can mean a period or epoch, and an era is a historical period.

clue.text: Policemen stand around consuming a mince dish

indicators.note: to consume something takes it inside, so the police wrap round the a

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
taken as written
to loaf is to idle or stand around

explanation.surface: Police officers idle about while eating a minced-meat meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Meatloaf is a baked dish of minced meat shaped like a loaf.

clue.text: Picked up fungus and alga to compare

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so this goes by how it is said

blocks.note: a lichen is a partnership of a fungus and an alga

explanation.surface: A naturalist gathers a fungus and an alga to see how they differ.
explanation.walkthrough: Lichen is not a fungus and an alga side by side but one organism formed by both.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to draw a comparison between them.

clue.text: Go by front of orchard to get fruit

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: go and pep both mean energy or vigour
the first letter of orchard

explanation.surface: Walk past the front of an orchard to pick some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go by' reads as pass, but 'Go' is a noun meaning energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pepo is a fleshy fruit with a hard rind, such as a melon or pumpkin.

clue.text: Relaxes grants following student's departure

indicators.note: once the student departs, the letter standing for a learner is gone

blocks.note: to lease is to grant use of property
L is a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student's money is freed up after they leave college.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to loosen or slacken, so eases means relaxes.

clue.text: Delight if family houses pet

indicators.note: a house holds things inside it, so the letters lie within these words

blocks.note: letters running through these words

explanation.surface: A family delights in keeping an animal at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an animal, but it means a fit of sulking.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet in the old sense is a fit of pique, and a tiff is a petty quarrel.

clue.text: Tent's top cut off with sword

indicators.note: cutting off the top of a downward entry removes its first letter

blocks.note: a tepee is a conical tent

explanation.surface: Someone slices the top off a tent with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is a fencing weapon, a type of sword.

clue.text: Criminal stuck without leader of cartel after trouble somewhere in Russia

indicators.note: losing the leader of a word removes its first letter from the other word
criminal means crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

blocks.note: to irk is to annoy or trouble
taken as written, to be rearranged
the first letter of cartel

explanation.surface: A gangster trapped after a drug cartel loses its boss, somewhere in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' reads as a noun for the gangster, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Irkutsk is a large city in Siberia, an example of a place in Russia.

clue.text: Setter's beyond old painting technique

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as I, so setter's is I'm
past means beyond, as in past the gate
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler claims to be too old for a certain painting method.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is a method of laying paint on thickly so brush strokes stand out.

clue.text: Men going after mink, say, causes outrage

blocks.note: mink is an example of a fur
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers, placed after

explanation.surface: Men chasing after mink stoles cause a public scandal, as with anti-fur protests.
explanation.definitionFit: A furor is an outburst of public anger or excitement, an uproar.

clue.text: Snoop around new senator's bunk

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the snooping word wraps round the rest

blocks.note: to nose about is to snoop
N is the abbreviation for new
Sen is the abbreviation for senator

explanation.surface: A spy pokes around a newly elected senator's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' suggests a bed, but it is short for bunkum, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk, short for bunkum, means foolish talk, the same as nonsense.
